gates.summary: Live tiles follow the model's tile geometry (late selection, partial edges, stage changes); completed comparisons stay responsive while another job runs; folder jobs save together; queue estimates separate measured from unmeasured work.
gates.next_action: Repeat the recorded cases on each new package.

gates.summary: The macOS beta is Developer ID signed, notarized and stapled. Images, video, cancellation, worker recovery, the in-app update and the system-codec route passed on an M1 Pro.
gates.next_action: Keep the accepted hashes; re-run the trust checks on every new build.

gates.summary: The beta feed is live on the website. Downloads are verified by size, SHA-256 and minisign signature; truncated and substituted archives are rejected; settings, recipes and the queue are backed up before an install.
gates.next_action: Publish every future entry only after installing it from the feed on a test machine.

gates.summary: A complete five-minute 480p clip exported at 2x on ROCm (9,000 frames, audio intact); a six-frame 4K to 8K export and recovery from a forced output-size failure passed.
gates.next_action: Keep the workload limits documented; a full 4K export of several minutes has not been exercised.

gates.summary: NAFNet and SPAN can diverge on some inputs. Bounded retries and a pre-quantization guard reject unstable output instead of saving it; two of eleven reproduced scans are rejected.
gates.next_action: Document the rejection limit and keep the originals.

gates.summary: Every catalog download names its author, source and license. NomosWebPhoto and HFA2k download under the author's CC BY 4.0 terms with attribution; the two HAT face checkpoints require a verified user import; no weights are bundled.
gates.next_action: Keep the notices in sync with the catalog.

gates.summary: The Windows CPU, DirectML and NVIDIA CUDA installers are built on GitHub-hosted runners (windows-installers.yml) with the licensing-clean media runtime (MSYS2 UCRT64 plus MSVC) and are attached to a release only after verify_codec_allowlist, the NVIDIA redistribution policy, an installed-package smoke test and the architecture check pass; each ships its corresponding source, and the CUDA engine ships as verified parts beside its installer. All three passed on the release branch in run 42411586091, on an earlier commit than the final candidate. As the beta policy in docs/platforms.md says, they are not code-signed, and DirectML and CUDA are published labelled untested.
gates.next_action: Run the workflow on the final candidate commit and attach only what it verified.

gates.summary: The Linux CPU, AMD ROCm and NVIDIA CUDA AppImages are built on Ubuntu 22.04 GitHub-hosted runners (linux-appimages.yml) and are attached to a release only after verify_codec_allowlist, the NVIDIA redistribution policy, an installed-package smoke test, the architecture check, AppImageHub's glibc ceiling of 2.35 and an offline window test pass; each ships corresponding source including Ubuntu sources for every bundled host library. The ROCm AppImage carries Ubuntu's own libnuma and libelf in place of the AlmaLinux copies in PyTorch's wheel. All three passed on the release branch in run 42499281378, before the stricter glibc and window checks (3965075, 310d64b). CUDA is published labelled untested. On a Radeon RX 9060 XT (ROCm 7.2, Fedora 44) the packaged worker of the ROCm AppImage from run 42499281378 passed scripts/acceptance_worker.py 6/6, with the AppImage's own library path as its AppRun sets it; the full desktop checks ran there in earlier builds.
gates.next_action: Run the workflow on the final candidate commit and attach only what it verified; repeat the full desktop checks with the ROCm AppImage on the RX 9060 XT.

gates.summary: The maintainer decided on 2026-11-08 to publish v0.3.1-beta like v0.3.0-beta: through the website, the update feed and GitHub Releases, macOS signed and notarized, the Windows installers not code-signed, and CUDA and DirectML labelled untested. The Microsoft Store listing is a separate, open decision (windows-signing-and-store).

Windows betas downloaded from the website or GitHub are not Authenticode-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first start. The Microsoft Store listing (HerRei.LocalSR) is not published. The Store route needs no own certificate (Microsoft signs the package after certification, docs/microsoft-store.md), but one x64 Store identity cannot choose the CPU, DirectML or CUDA worker, so its engine delivery is undecided.
gates.next_action: Decide how the Store package delivers its engine, and whether the direct downloads get a free open-source signature (SignPath Foundation needs builds on GitHub-hosted runners, which the release workflows now use).

gates.summary: Maintainer assessment without legal counsel (17 September 2026) in docs/licensing-media.md: demuxing, a user-installed FFmpeg, MPEG-2/AC-3 expiry and OS codecs are settled or negligible; NVIDIA's terms were assessed as low risk on the same basis as Intel's MKL, and the CUDA packages are published, labelled untested.
gates.next_action: Put the open questions to a lawyer before a stable release.

gates.summary: NVIDIA CUDA (published, labelled untested), Linux Intel XPU (withheld) and DirectML adapters other than the UHD 620 have not run on physical hardware. On the UHD 620 with its 2020 driver, DirectML matched the CPU (93.7 dB, source build, 9 November 2026), while OpenVINO crashes inside the driver and the GPU preflight refuses it.
gates.next_action: Collect volunteer hardware reports before describing these engines as tested.

gates.summary: HDR preservation, SeedVR2 3B, de-flicker and video face processing ship as Labs features. Perceptual HDR quality and long-clip temporal stability are unverified.
gates.next_action: Recommend short clips and state the memory and time limits in the app.
